description:
The place began as a manor court enclosed by a stone wall, which is why it was called "the stone yard"; the court is first mentioned around 1370 in a list of Leuchtenberg fiefs. From 1509 it belonged to the Kynšperk estate, which was confiscated from the town of Kynšperk after the Battle of White Mountain in 1620 and held by the Metternich family until 1726.

The present château is late Baroque. Hrady.cz says the town of Kynšperk had it built in the late 18th century on the site of an already demolished fortified manor, while the hotel says a new château went up in the northern part of the court around the turn of the 18th and 19th centuries and was completed by August Eusebius Haas, who bought the estate in 1840, so sources differ on who built it and when.

After the Second World War the army used the château; it was then left empty, vandalised and reduced to a ruin. In 2004 a private investor bought it and had it restored using historical materials, together with the park. It now operates as a château hotel with a restaurant, a wellness area and a park with a pond, in the West Bohemian Spa Triangle between Karlovy Vary, Františkovy Lázně and Mariánské Lázně.

faqs.question: How old is Kamenný Dvůr Château?
faqs.answer: The estate goes back to a manor court mentioned around 1370; the present late Baroque château dates from around the turn of the 19th century, and sources differ on the exact date.

faqs.question: Can you stay at the château?
faqs.answer: Yes. It operates as a hotel with a restaurant and a wellness area, after a restoration that began when a private investor bought the ruin in 2004.

meta_description: Stay at Kamenný Dvůr Château near Kynšperk nad Ohří, Czech Republic — a late Baroque château in the West Bohemian Spa Triangle. From approx. €110/night.

hotel.room_location_note: Rooms are at the château, Kamenný Dvůr 1; ask the hotel which building your room is in
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** Kamenný Dvůr is part of Kynšperk nad Ohří, about 11 km west of Sokolov and 15 km east of Cheb according to Hrady.cz, next to the R6 expressway at the Kynšperk turn-off; Booking lists free private parking.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €110/night for a 20 m² Standard Double Room on a high floor with a view, a private bathroom, a flat-screen TV and free Wi-Fi, with breakfast included on the non-refundable rate seen; a free-cancellation rate was around €122 and included two hours of spa a day and a parking spot, and a Deluxe Double Room was around €174. Booking showed a small tax charge (about €1) separately and some member-only discounts that are not included here.

**On-site:** A restaurant, a wellness area with a small thermal pool according to VisitCzechia, a park with a pond and an island, and free parking.

**Good to know:** Rates were seen for one February 2027 stay, a low-season date, so check your own dates on Booking. Sources differ on who built the château and when, and on its star rating.

**Combine with:** Teplá Monastery and the Bečov nad Teplou Château are within easy reach, according to VisitCzechia. [More castle hotels in Czech Republic](/castle-hotels/czech-republic).
